deltas.summary: Whether the semiclassical-to-memory-burdened transition in an evaporating black hole is practically instantaneous is the recognized crux of the primordial-black-hole dark matter debate, and it is genuinely unresolved. The affirmative case is an induction: black holes are saturons, and if [[claim:a20b90c8-66a7-47e6-b341-f3864098b28f|prototype saturon systems show decay suppression setting in sharply once roughly half the information is lost]], then the black hole transition should be step-like too. But the sharpness of that prototype onset has not itself been established, and the program's own proposal paper adopts the instantaneous transition as a modeling choice while stating that behavior past the burden threshold is not known. On the other side, no derivation of the emission rate across the transition exists per [[claim:72fa72e8-841c-4830-b018-432644c9a735|the absence of any derivation]], and independent constraint analyses in 2025 and 2026 treat the instantaneous transition as an idealization to be relaxed: parameterizing smooth crossovers around [[claim:cd14d3da-0fbb-4ffd-b679-55deeedd3aaa|the half-entropy-plus-order-one-percent onset bound]], they find persistent Hawking emission through the epochs that constrain primordial black holes, closing the light-PBH dark matter window per [[claim:65f3b122-10de-46ec-907c-e4543c78dc83|the BBN and recombination constraint result]]. The verdict is contested: a credible program asserts sharp onset on prototype evidence, credible independent work treats smoothness as the realistic or conservative case, and the question would be decided by either a derivation of the rate across the transition or direct evidence on how sharply suppression sets in in prototype simulations.
